target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in az login
target.body:
## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers for interactive `az login --use-device-code`
- reject through a single guarded failure path and terminate the az child process on stream failure
- cover stdout and stderr stream errors with a focused CLI regression test
- collision check: no open PR found for the Microsoft Foundry az login stream-error issue or `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts`

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 1 test passed

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Microsoft Foundry forwarded `az login` stdout/stderr `data` to the terminal but did not handle readable stream `error`, so an `EPIPE` could escape the login promise.
Real environment tested: mocked Azure CLI child process using Node `PassThrough` streams in Vitest; no real Azure CLI login was required.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: emitted `error` on mocked `az login` stdout and stderr streams after starting `azLoginDeviceCodeWithOptions`.
Evidence after fix: each emitted stream error did not throw out of band, rejected the login promise with `az login <stream> stream failed: EPIPE`, and sent `SIGTERM` to the child process.
Observed result after fix: az login stream failures are reported to the caller as login failures instead of unhandled stream errors.
What was not tested: full CI and an interactive live Azure device-code login.
